title: Merit order and electricity prices
summary: How a power market sets one price from the marginal plant, why residual load (load minus wind and solar) is the variable that matters, and what shapes the supply curve.

concepts.label: Day-ahead electricity price
concepts.description: The price of the DE-LU bidding zone's day-ahead auction per quarter-hour, in EUR/MWh; uniform for all accepted bids.

facts.text: Energy-Charts serves SMARD.de's day-ahead prices under CC BY 4.0.
Single day-ahead coupling (SDAC) clears Europe's bidding zones together in one auction.

children.label: Negative price
children.description: Hours when generators pay to deliver: must-run plants and output-based subsidies keep running when supply exceeds demand.

children.label: Marginal cost
children.description: The running cost of one more MWh from a plant (fuel, CO₂, operation); the bid a plant makes in a competitive market.

facts.text: Gas plants' marginal cost moves with the TTF gas price and the EU ETS CO₂ price.

concepts.label: Merit order
concepts.description: Plants sorted by marginal cost into a supply curve; the demand that must be met picks the last plant needed, whose cost sets the price.

facts.text: The merit-order effect: renewables with near-zero marginal cost shift the supply curve right and lower prices.

children.label: Residual load
children.description: Load minus wind and solar output: the demand left for dispatchable plants and imports.

children.label: Supply curve convexity
children.description: How the slope of price against residual load grows as costlier plants are needed.

children.label: Bids and the auction (EUPHEMIA)
children.description: The actual stepwise bid curves of the auction, which the binned curve only estimates.

concepts.label: Generation by source
concepts.description: Public net generation per source in MW per quarter-hour (ENTSO-E data via Energy-Charts).

children.label: Variable renewables
children.description: Wind and solar: near-zero marginal cost, output set by the weather.

children.label: Dispatchable plants
children.description: Lignite, hard coal, gas, pumped hydro: output set by the market. Gas and pumped hydro are typically marginal.

children.label: Cross-border trade
children.description: Net imports (positive) or exports; neighbours' plants are part of the same coupled merit order.

concepts.label: Duck curve
concepts.description: The midday dip in residual load (and price) as solar output peaks, followed by a steep evening ramp.

facts.text: The name comes from CAISO's 2013 chart of California's net load.

concepts.label: Fuel and CO₂ prices
concepts.description: Gas (TTF) and EU ETS allowance prices shift the whole curve up or down; not in this data.
